title: Iblis asks for time
hookLine: Iblis refuses again and asks for respite to mislead, except the sincere (38:71–83)

lines: THE ONE WHO WOULD NOT BOW.
cards: Adam made from clay, the angels told to bow, and one who refused. Iblis, saying I'm better than him: You made me from fire and him from clay. This path met the scene back on day twenty-four, and the lesson was pride.
Surah Sad tells it again, and lets it run a few lines further, past the refusal, into a negotiation. Iblis, expelled, doesn't beg to come back. He asks for something else.
Time. And in his own boast, he admits there's someone he can't touch.

teach.h: HE ASKS FOR TIME, NOT FORGIVENESS.
teach.b: Verses seventy-one to seventy-six give the refusal: I am better than him. Then seventy-seven and seventy-eight: go out from here, you are rejected, and My curse is on you until the Day of Judgment. Verse seventy-nine.
Iblis says: my Lord, then give me respite until the day they are raised. Notice two things.
He still says my Lord; he doesn't deny Allah exists, he refuses Him. And he doesn't ask for forgiveness. He asks for time, to use against the people he refused to bow to.
Allah answers: you are of those given respite, until the day of the known time. Then the boast, verses eighty-two and eighty-three.
He swears by Allah's own might that he'll mislead every one of them, and then he adds the exception himself.
Pickthall: "Save Thy single-minded slaves among them." The Arabic is al-mukhlasin, those made sincere, purified.
The word is recited two ways in the established readings of the Qur'an: mukhlasin, those Allah has made sincere, and mukhlisin, those who make their worship sincere.
Some scholars hold both meanings at once: sincerity is something a person works at, and something given. Either way, the enemy names his own limit. He can whisper to anyone.
He can't take someone whose devotion is single-minded, done for Allah alone, not for an audience.
The surah closes soon after with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ told to say: I ask no payment for this, and I'm not one who pretends. Sincerity, at the start and at the end.

how: Muslims speak of ikhlas, sincerity, as doing every act for Allah alone, and many renew their intention (niyya) before prayer, charity and other good deeds.

o: those made sincere, whom Iblis says he can't mislead
the angels who bowed down when Adam was made
the scribes who first wrote down the revealed verses

games.q: Iblis in Surah Sad — tap the pairs.

s: in Surah Sad, Iblis denies that Allah exists
he still says my Lord, and swears by Allah's might; he refuses, he doesn't deny.
Iblis himself names the people he can't mislead
save Your single-minded servants, he says in 38:83.
mukhlasin is recited only one way
established readings have mukhlasin and mukhlisin, made sincere and making sincere.

games.q: you're Iblis, just expelled for refusing to bow. what do you ask for?
o: respite until the day they are raised.
games.why: he asked for time, not forgiveness, to use against Adam's children, and was given it until the known day.

practice: Choose one small thing you'll do today, a kindness, a task, a prayer if you pray, and look at the reason you're doing it. If part of it is for someone to notice, gently set that part down.
Imagine doing it with no one ever knowing, only God, or only you, and see whether it feels lighter or harder.

wordCard.voice: Al-mukhlasin, those made sincere, the one group Iblis admits, in his own boast, that he can never mislead. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: those made sincere, purified; also recited mukhlisin, those who make their worship sincere.

carryVoice: Your line: the sincere are protected. Even Iblis, in his own boast, names that limit. Rest well.

sources.q: Save Thy single-minded slaves among them.

sources.ref: the canonical readings (qira'at) of mukhlasin / mukhlisin
